title: Real-Time Computer Vision & Edge AI with OpenCV & ONNX (PYTH_192_S1 to PYTH_192_S8)

slides.title: OpenCV Pipeline & Edge Inference
slides.prompt: Edge AI processing pipelines capture video streams, preprocess frames as NumPy arrays, and execute optimized ONNX model inference.
slides.codeSnippet:
import cv2
import onnxruntime as ort

session = ort.InferenceSession('model.onnx')
cap = cv2.VideoCapture(0)
ret, frame = cap.read()

slides.title: Color Space Conversion
slides.prompt: Fill in the OpenCV function used to convert continuous video frame color spaces (e.g., BGR to RGB).

slides.title: ONNX Runtime Execution Providers
slides.prompt: How does ONNX Runtime achieve accelerated inference on specialized edge hardware (e.g., TensorRT, OpenVINO)?
options: By attaching target-specific Execution Providers that offload subgraph operators to hardware accelerators
By recompiling Python source code into native dynamic C libraries
By converting images into 1D text formats before processing
By increasing the video stream frame rate programmatically
slides.correctAnswer: By attaching target-specific Execution Providers that offload subgraph operators to hardware accelerators

slides.title: Image Resizing for Neural Models
slides.prompt: Fill in the OpenCV function used to scale captured video frames to match model tensor dimensions.

slides.title: Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS)
slides.prompt: What role does Non-Maximum Suppression play in object detection pipelines (e.g., YOLO)?
options: It filters out overlapping redundant bounding boxes, keeping only high-confidence detections
It increases the brightness and contrast of low-light video frames
It converts RGB color channels to grayscale matrices
It compresses the output ONNX model file size on disk
slides.correctAnswer: It filters out overlapping redundant bounding boxes, keeping only high-confidence detections

slides.title: Drawing Bounding Boxes
slides.prompt: Fill in the OpenCV function used to render bounding box overlays on image frames.

slides.title: Model Quantization (INT8)
slides.prompt: What is the trade-off when applying INT8 quantization to an FP32 neural network model for edge deployment?
options: Significantly smaller model size and faster inference at the cost of slight precision/accuracy loss
Higher floating-point precision at the cost of double memory usage
Slower processing time with complete loss of color information
Eliminating the need for video input hardware
slides.correctAnswer: Significantly smaller model size and faster inference at the cost of slight precision/accuracy loss

slides.title: Releasing Video Capture
slides.prompt: Fill in the OpenCV method used to free camera hardware locks when exiting a processing loop.
